incidents.title: Microsoft: Jasper Sleet uses Faceswap and voice changers for fake IT workers
incidents.targets: Western employers hiring remote IT staff
incidents.confidenceReason: Microsoft Threat Intelligence names Faceswap and voice-changing software.
incidents.summary: Since 2024 the workers used AI to swap faces into stolen identity documents and make headshots, and voice changers in interviews. A March 2026 Microsoft report describes AI use at every stage of hiring.
incidents.quote: use AI tools like Faceswap to move their pictures over to the stolen employment and identity documents
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Microsoft has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

incidents.title: BlueNoroff uses deepfaked executives in Zoom call to infect crypto employee
incidents.actor: BlueNoroff / TA444 / Sapphire Sleet (Huntress: STARDUST CHOLLIMA)
incidents.outcome: Eight malicious binaries installed including keylogger and wallet hijacker.
incidents.confidenceReason: Huntress incident analysis reports deepfaked leadership on the call; deepfake evidence is the victim account.
incidents.summary: A Telegram and Calendly lure led to a fake Zoom with deepfakes of known leaders who told the victim to install an extension, which was a malicious AppleScript. Huntress investigated in June 2025.

incidents.title: Deepfake Zoom call impersonating a trusted contact leads to malware and account takeover of a crypto analyst
incidents.targets: Cryptocurrency analyst Mai Fujimoto (X, Telegram, MetaMask accounts)
incidents.outcome: The victim believes malware was installed and accounts were taken over.
incidents.confidenceReason: The deepfake rests on the victim's own account; no investigator has confirmed it.

incidents.quote: Cryptocurrency analyst Mai Fujimoto reported losing access to her X, Telegram, and MetaMask accounts through a video call with a purported deepfake impersonating a trusted contact.
incidents.singleSourceReason: This operation reaches the ledger only through AI Incident Database's record; the 2026-11-17 sweep found no other publisher.

incidents.title: Impostor uses AI voice of Marco Rubio on Signal
incidents.targets: Three foreign ministers, a US governor, a member of Congress
incidents.outcome: At least five non-Department individuals contacted; State Dept said no direct cyber threat to its systems.
incidents.confidenceReason: The cable counts as a primary source, reached through CBS, but its only verbatim sentence about AI is hedged: the impostor "likely aimed to manipulate targeted individuals using AI-generated text and voice messages". NPR attributes the AI link to "two senior officials and a cable" without quoting it. The cable's own wording supports Strong, not Confirmed.
incidents.summary: A Signal account named like Rubio left AI voice messages for officials. The cable linked it to a May 2025 FBI-investigated impersonation.
incidents.quote: likely aimed to manipulate targeted individuals using AI-generated text and voice messages, with the goal of gaining access to information or accounts

incidents.title: Russian-speaking actor builds ScopeCreep multi-stage Go malware with ChatGPT
incidents.targets: Gamers who downloaded a trojanized Crosshair-X tool
incidents.outcome: OpenAI banned the accounts; the malware was spread through a trojanized gaming tool.
incidents.confidenceReason: OpenAI, the model provider, states the actor used its models to build and debug the malware.
incidents.summary: A Russian-speaking actor used throwaway ChatGPT accounts, one per small change, to develop and refine multi-stage Windows malware in Go, debug it and set up its command-and-control. The date is the report month.
incidents.quote: This actor used our models to assist with developing and refining Windows malware, debugging code across multiple languages, and setting up their command-and-control infrastructure.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only OpenAI has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep, which AI Adoption and AI Threat Watch restate.

incidents.title: Cambodia-based task scam uses ChatGPT to write lures in six languages
incidents.targets: UK mobile users recruited via SMS, WhatsApp and Telegram
incidents.outcome: Responders were routed from SMS to WhatsApp to a Telegram 'mentor'; one lure reached an OpenAI staffer.
incidents.confidenceReason: OpenAI, the model provider, reports on its own platform in June 2025: "Scam: Operation 'Wrong Number' ... We banned ChatGPT accounts that were generating short recruitment-style messages in English, Spanish, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, German, and Haitian Creole."
incidents.summary: A centralized Cambodia-based operation used ChatGPT to generate recruitment-style task-scam messages in six languages.
incidents.quote: A centralised Cambodia-based operation generated recruitment-style messages in six languages offering pay for trivial tasks, routing responders from SMS to WhatsApp to a Telegram mentor; one lure hit an OpenAI staffer.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only OpenAI has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep, which AI Threat Watch restates.
